raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Depends on #1929; the follow-up itself adds the existing D512 flavor to the per-tensor FP8 graph split domain. Standalone already supports this split kernel, while an otherwise identical graph plan was rejected by `split_d_shapes`.

Dense D512 and its existing 16-aligned head envelope now use the same FP32 partials and final combine through the graph API, with O scaling, Stats and Amax, including sink composition from #1929. Scheduler, CGA, scalar-tail, paged and packed-Q constraints stay in place. No kernel body, heuristics or placement change. The support tracker and the previous packed-domain decline detector are updated.

Validation on SM100, 148 SM / 600 W, cuDNN9.27.0.42, CuTeDSL4.8.0:

- RED before admission; 33 graph/domain cases pass after. Covers exact D512 and D384x320 envelope, both FP8 inputs, all four output dtypes, packed/unpacked GQA, empty split chunks, padded output storage, sinks, rebind and changed-input capture replay.
- Targeted envelope/FP8-output/sink memcheck: zero errors. All 32 new cases are collected by the normal FROST folder and CI filters.
- Four same-feature B2 H4/KH2 KV8192 cases, Q1/Q17 with/without sink: 72 explicit plans check full O/Stats/Amax before/after timed replay. New split plans take 35.2%–48.8% of the best measured unsplit latency, improving in both candidate orders. Includes all three legal schedulers in correctness checks. These are warmed local CUDA-graph measurements, not default-selection or serving claims.

Incorporated parent review fix21ef93447 in4d7a38d59: serial combine masks zero-weight partial payloads. Parent307 regressions pass. This PR's unchanged four-cell/72-plan performance probe was also rerun after the update, with full O/Stats/Amax checks before/after replay; all four cells still improve in both candidate orders.

Parent #1929 is now merged into this branch. The complete source tree is identical to the qualified pre-merge tree; this update changes ancestry only.

This capability expansion can change automatic first-plan selection even though heuristic and placement source files are unchanged. Review reproduced a slower first plan for B2, Hq/Hkv4/2, Q257, KV8192, D512, E4M3 inputs/BF16 output without a sink. The explicit split capability remains useful for the measured short-Q region; the first-candidate regression is handed to the heuristics owner for policy qualification. See the nonblocking P2 in https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1930#pullrequestreview-5666421562.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""The existing FP8 D512 split kernel is also reachable through graph plans."""
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from frost_test_utils import requires_dsl, requires_pre_rubin_blackwell
+import test_sdpa_prepared_fp8 as shared
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_dsl, requires_pre_rubin_blackwell]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d,dv", [(512, 512), (384, 320)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("output", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e5m2])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "sink,split,pack,dtype",
+    [(False, 2, False, torch.float8_e4m3fn), (False, 9, True, torch.float8_e5m2), (True, 4, True, torch.float8_e4m3fn), (True, 9, False, torch.float8_e5m2)],
+)
+def test_d512_fp8_graph_split_rebind_replay(d, dv, output, sink, split, pack, dtype):
+    sinks = torch.linspace(-12, 12, 4, device="cuda").view(1, 4, 1, 1) if sink else None
+    g, vp, ws, bufs, tensors = shared._case(d=d, dv=dv, sq=17, skv=256, split_kv=split, dtype=dtype, output_dtype=output, sink=sinks, output_padding=16)
+    selected = g.plans[g._plan_index]
+    g.create_execution_plan(selected.engine_id, replace(selected.knobs, pack_gqa=pack, sched_policy=0))
+    g.select_plan(len(g.plans) - 1)
+    g.check_support()
+    g.build_plans()
+    ws = torch.empty(max(1, g.get_workspace_size()), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    assert g._compiled_plans[g._plan_index]._prepared.spec.split == split
+    for iteration in range(2):
+        if iteration:
+            for name in ("q", "k", "v", "lse", "amax_o", "descale_q", "scale_o") + (("sinks",) if sink else ()):
+                bufs[name] = bufs[name].clone()
+                vp[tensors[name]] = bufs[name]
+            bufs["o_storage"] = torch.full_like(bufs["o_storage"], 12)
+            bufs["o"] = bufs["o_storage"][..., :dv].transpose(1, 2)
+            vp[tensors["o"]] = bufs["o"]
+            bufs["descale_q"].fill_(0.5)
+            bufs["scale_o"].fill_(1.9)
+            ws = torch.empty_like(ws)
+        g.execute(vp, ws)
+        shared._check(bufs, thd=False, sq=17, skv=256)
+        with shared._cuda_graph() as capture:
+            with torch.cuda.graph(capture):
+                g.execute(vp, ws)
+            if sink:
+                bufs["sinks"].fill_(5 if iteration else -3)
+            bufs["descale_q"].fill_(0.7)
+            for name in ("o", "lse", "amax_o"):
+                bufs[name].fill_(float("nan"))
+            capture.replay()
+            shared._check(bufs, thd=False, sq=17, skv=256)
+        assert torch.all(bufs["o_storage"][..., dv:] == 12)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `4d7a38d59683` against base `584a4c6eb08c`.

The D512 graph integration passed correctness and rebinding/replay validation. One nonblocking P2 remains: this capability addition also changes automatic plan selection, and the newly selected split regresses a measured prefill shape. The inherited zero-weight sink fix is present and its regressions pass. This is an author-account review; independent approval remains required.

**[P2] Keep automatic D512 splitting within a qualified region** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/4d7a38d59683678fed12bda0413409eac0abb07d/python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/engines.py#L2849))

Adding (512, 512) here also enables heuristics._split_points(), which puts its chosen split first. The change therefore affects the default plan, despite the description's statement that placement is unchanged. With FROST enabled, dense E4M3 Q/K/V, BF16 O, B=2, Hq/Hkv=4/2, Q=257, KV=8192, D=512 and no sink, the actual first graph plan changes from split=1 on parent 21ef93447 to split=4 here. On a local SM100 engineering device (148 SMs, 600 W), warmed CUDA-graph replay rises from 116.2 to 203.7 us (+75%); host enqueue separately rises from 17.4 to 19.0 us. O/Stats/Amax pass on both. Six alternating same-process rounds independently reproduce the replay difference (116.4 versus 203.7 us). Please preserve the explicit split capability while keeping automatic selection unsplit outside a measured region, or qualify/correct the D512 cost model and add first-candidate coverage. Short-Q cases improve, so this is a localized selection issue, not a reason to drop the new capability. Also update the scope description to acknowledge the default-selection effect.

Evidence: Actual parent and current source imports, identical native extension sources, cuDNN 9.27/CuTe DSL 4.8, six warmed 100-replay samples per source; a separate old/new-capability comparison alternated execution order on identical inputs. Public graph first plan was index 0 in both revisions. CPU enqueue measured separately with synchronization outside the timed region. Attribution: Newly exposed by this PR: the existing split cost model was previously gated off for this graph flavor.

Validation: SM100: 132 selected native tests passed, zero skips: 32 new D512 graph cases, 82 parent sink-split cases, 2 sink-free quantized ABI controls and 16 native paged-binding cases. Source import and matching native extension were verified. Independent D384/V320 multiwave probe: B=8, Q=1024, KV=512, split=9 with a sink; all three schedulers with PackGQA on/off passed O/Stats/Amax reference checks. Three identical-input executions per configuration were bit-identical for those outputs. Six first-candidate comparison cells: five sink-free cells changed split selection; the sink control remained unsplit. Short-Q cells improved, while the Q=257 cell above reliably regressed. Performance is warmed local replay/host submission, not serving throughput. Requested focused python/sdpa/frost CI for this head; it is pending, not counted as passing validation.

Limitations: Independent execution and performance coverage is SM100 only; no SM103 validation or broader workload performance claim. Same-configuration repeatability checks do not establish invariance across split counts, hardware or software versions.

Comment only: GitHub does not allow reviewing one's own PR with approval/request-changes.
